skill.name: browser-discovery
skill.description: Selects available browser automation tools to discover links on JavaScript-rendered documentation sites when static retrieval is insufficient.
skill.summary: Selects browser automation tools and discovers links on JavaScript-rendered documentation sites.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: All 31 static findings are false positives caused by documentation URLs, loopback checks, /dev/null, WSL host addressing, or Markdown backticks. One medium-risk issue remains: the troubleshooting guide executes an unpinned @playwright/mcp@latest package through npx.

remediation.suggestion: Replace @latest with a reviewed version and avoid -y. Require user confirmation before downloading or executing the package.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The troubleshooting guide runs `npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --help`, which downloads and executes the current package release without version pinning or confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command explicitly selects @latest and uses -y, so npx can download and execute an unreviewed release without an interactive approval step.

content.value_statement: JavaScript-rendered documentation can hide links from static fetches. This skill selects available browser tools and extracts structured navigation after pages render.
actual_capabilities: Detects available Antigravity, Cursor, or Playwright browser tooling before use.
Determines when static curl retrieval is insufficient for JavaScript-rendered documentation.
Navigates documentation sites and waits for client-side content to render.
Extracts navigation links from accessibility snapshots or browser results.
Provides fallback instructions for browser startup, connectivity checks, and tool failures.
limitations: Requires an installed browser integration; it does not bundle browser software or the referenced Playwright wrapper.
Depends on site availability, rendering behavior, authentication, and access permissions.
Hardcoded examples use docs.viperjuice.dev and must be replaced with the intended documentation site.
Does not define crawl deduplication, robots compliance, or full content indexing.

use_cases.title: Select an Available Browser

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Web Content

prompt_templates.title: Check Browser Need
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether {documentation_url} needs browser automation. Try static retrieval first, detect available browser tools, and report the recommended method.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for one documentation homepage.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Navigation Links
prompt_templates.prompt: Discover navigation links on {documentation_url}. Use the best available browser tool, wait for rendering, and return page titles, URLs, and sections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when static retrieval misses navigation.

prompt_templates.title: Map Documentation Sections
prompt_templates.prompt: Map up to {max_pages} pages from {documentation_url}. Expand collapsed navigation, use accessibility snapshots, group pages by section, and note rendering failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a structured documentation inventory.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Discovery Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit documentation discovery for {documentation_url} across curl and available browser tools. Compare coverage, identify dynamic routes, deduplicate links, and explain unresolved gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this to evaluate discovery quality across tools.

best_practices: Try static retrieval before browser automation unless configuration explicitly requires JavaScript rendering.
Prefer accessibility snapshots for structured links and use screenshots only when visual layout matters.
Limit page scope, wait for rendering, and close browser sessions after discovery.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a browser tool exists before checking the current environment.
Do not navigate authenticated or sensitive sites without explicit permission and an approved browser profile.
Do not execute unpinned packages or expose Chrome debugging beyond trusted local interfaces.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when static retrieval returns little content, receives a forbidden response, or misses navigation rendered by JavaScript.

faq.question: Which browser tools does it support?
faq.answer: It documents Antigravity browser_subagent, Cursor browser tools, cursor-agent, and a Playwright wrapper connected to Chrome debugging.

faq.question: Does the skill install Playwright or Chrome?
faq.answer: No. The required browser, integration, and wrapper must already exist or be installed separately.

faq.question: What output does it produce?
faq.answer: It returns discovered page URLs, titles, section labels, navigation structure, and whether JavaScript rendering was required.

faq.question: Can it access authenticated documentation?
faq.answer: Only when the selected browser profile already has approved access. Users should avoid exposing credentials or unrelated session data.

faq.question: Why are accessibility snapshots preferred?
faq.answer: Snapshots provide structured text, roles, and link targets that are easier to parse than screenshots.
